output.answer: Yes. CDW confirmed in July 2026 that it had made organizational changes that included job cuts, telling CRN it made 'coworker reductions' to sharpen operating discipline and reinvest in its highest-return opportunities as part of its AI-first 'Geared for Growth' cost-savings drive (targeting $100M-$200M in run-rate savings into 2027-2028). CDW did not disclose how many employees were affected. This is the company's latest in a series of layoff rounds: it cut workers again in July 2025 (its fourth round in two years, per Crain's Chicago Business) and laid off between 450 and 750 employees in April 2023. As of its Q3 2026 earnings call (Nov. 4, 2026), CDW reported 14,600 total coworkers.
caveats: CDW declined to disclose the number of employees affected in the July 2026 round or which units were cut, so the scale of the layoffs is unconfirmed; the July 2026 round was reported by CRN based on sources plus a company statement.

CDW has not framed these actions as a single announced mass-layoff program; its statement described 'organizational changes' that 'included coworker reductions', and it has not filed a specific headcount reduction figure publicly.
Headcount (14,600 coworkers) reflects Q3 2026 and includes ~600 coworkers added via the Lovelytics acquisition, so net headcount trends mix layoffs with acquisitions.

These changes further position CDW to continue delivering the outcomes our customers need and expect in the AI era,” the statement said.
CDW in July initiated a round of layoffs, sources told CRN. ... The company did not disclose the number of impacted employees.

CDW CEO Christine Leahy told analysts Wednesday that the company’s ‘Geared For Growth’ AI-first initiative, which is targeting cost savings of up to $200 million, will “supercharge” the company as it embeds AI throughout the $23.2 billion organization.
CDW cuts more workers in fourth round of layoffs over 2 years

Coworker count totaled 14,600, while customer-facing coworker count was approximately 10,500. Our headcount in the quarter reflects the addition of approximately 600 new coworkers from the Lovelytics acquisition.

CDW did not disclose the number of employees affected by the July 2026 layoffs; the possibility of layoffs had been raised on the Q1 2026 earnings call in May.
The layoffs come as CDW pursues its 'Geared For Growth' AI-first initiative, targeting $100M-$200M in run-rate cost savings/improvements into 2027-2028.
In July 2025, CDW cut more workers in what Crain's Chicago Business reported was the fourth round of layoffs over two years.
